reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g2_mg_q4_3), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample set fully addresses the competency requirements of identifying and distinguishing straight lines, curved lines, flat surfaces, and curved surfaces of 3-dimensional objects. Straight and curved lines are tested via items such as "The edge of a ruler never bends. Is it a straight line or a curved line?" and "The rim of a circle bends all the way around. Is it a straight line or a curved line?". Flat and curved surfaces of solid objects are tested in questions like "Which best describes the side of a solid figure that you could trace with a straight ruler?" and "A solid figure has a surface that bends all the way around, like a ball. What kind of surface is that?".

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Coverage spans both dimensional domains targeted by the standard: lines (straight vs. curved) and 3D surfaces (flat vs. curved). Real-world and geometric objects including a ruler ("The edge of a ruler never bends. Is it a straight line or a curved line?"), a circle ("The rim of a circle bends all the way around. Is it a straight line or a curved line?"), a ball ("A solid figure has a surface that bends all the way around, like a ball. What kind of surface is that?"), and a cylinder/can ("A can has both flat surfaces (its ends) and one other kind of surface. What kind is it?") are comprehensively represented.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The problems are appropriately targeted for Grade 2 Quarter 4 students. The prompts use clear, descriptive everyday language such as "It bends smoothly and changes direction. Is it a straight line or a curved line?" and "The edge of a ruler never bends. Is it a straight line or a curved line?". The cognitive load is focused strictly on visual and tactile properties of lines and surfaces without unnecessary complexity.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The items test distinct perspectives and sub-skills: definition/property-based line identification ("It bends smoothly and changes direction. Is it a straight line or a curved line?"), boundary/rim identification ("The rim of a circle bends all the way around. Is it a straight line or a curved line?"), tactile/tracing identification of flat surfaces ("Which best describes the side of a solid figure that you could trace with a straight ruler?"), and multi-surface object analysis ("A can has both flat surfaces (its ends) and one other kind of surface. What kind is it?").

competency_alignment.rationale: All questions align directly with the MATATAG competency without introducing extraneous concepts or premature geometric definitions. Each question, whether focusing on straight/curved lines (e.g. "The edge of a ruler never bends. Is it a straight line or a curved line?") or 3D surfaces (e.g. "A solid figure has a surface that bends all the way around, like a ball. What kind of surface is that?"), stays strictly within the boundaries of identifying lines and surfaces.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The scale of difficulty, vocabulary, and conceptual depth is well-calibrated for Grade 2. Concrete exemplars like balls, cans, and rulers grounded in questions like "A can has both flat surfaces (its ends) and one other kind of surface. What kind is it?" provide intuitive access to 3D surface concepts suitable for 7-8 year old learners.
